title: Neuromodulation in Obesity
summary: Increasingly, it has been noted that the treatment of obesity and eating disorders must also involve the brain in order to progress in terms of effective therapeutic approaches. While neuromodulatory treatments generally are of broad interest in the context of obesity and eating behaviors, there is clearly a need for further empirically driven strategies to identify appropriate treatments to achieve clinically relevant changes. Therapeutic strategies utilizing noninvasive neuromodulation techniques could contribute to improving successful and stable weight loss, particularly when embedded in overarching conservative therapeutic approaches.Two such techniques are noninvasive brain stimulation, which achieves modulation of the brain's own rhythms by weak currents via sponge electrodes placed on the scalp, and neurofeedback, a voluntary manipulation of brain rhythms via a computerized task.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Obesity (BMI > 30 kg/m²)
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy and lactation, photosensitive epilepsy, electronic/ferromagnetic implantats, Diabetes mellitus Type 1/2
